zh:
从两部拉丁诗作打开罗马的世界开端：奥维德《变形记》卷一描述混合的物质如何分开、万物与人如何出现；《岁时记》卷一则让双面神雅努斯亲口解释自己与混沌、门槛和开端的关系。这里先收录这两种有明确文本边界的讲法，分别阅读与比较。

罗马宗教与神话受到意大利本土、伊特鲁里亚和希腊传统的共同影响。奥维德使用希腊神名、母题和哲学式的宇宙想象，并不意味着他的诗就是全部罗马人的共同信条；同一作者在不同作品中也会给出不同说明。地图的罗马点是这批拉丁文学材料的阅读入口，不代表宇宙故事发生于罗马，更不是古代文化分布的边界。

本次选编尚不覆盖完整的罗马诸神谱系、城市建城传说或帝国各地的地方祭祀。每条叙事附具体卷次与行号，雅努斯条目另列钱币实物，便于把文学讲述和图像证据分开看。
en:
Two Latin poems open this selection of Roman beginnings. Book 1 of Ovid's Metamorphoses describes the separation of mixed matter and the emergence of living creatures and humanity. Book 1 of his Fasti gives Janus a voice to explain his relationship to chaos, doorways and beginnings. These are two separately bounded literary accounts, available to read and compare without joining them into one sequence.

Roman religion drew on Italic, Etruscan and Greek traditions. Ovid's use of Greek figures, motifs and cosmological speculation does not make either poem a creed shared by every Roman; even the same poet offers different explanations in different works. The point at Rome is a gateway to these Latin texts, not the location where the cosmos was created or a boundary of ancient cultural distribution.

This initial selection does not cover the full Roman pantheon, foundation legends or local cults across the empire. Specific books and line ranges identify each account. The Janus entry also links a surviving coin so readers can distinguish literary narrative from material evidence.
